subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should OpenClaw permanently treat ClawHub, bundled metadata, and official-catalog mappings as acknowledgement-free sources while using the existing `--force` flag to acknowledge every other direct executable plugin source?
rationale: The implementation and proof can establish consistency, but code review cannot choose the permanent trust policy or decide whether breaking unattended arbitrary-source installs and broadening an existing public flag is the intended compatibility contract.

options.title: Approve the proposed boundary
options.body: Accept the current trusted-source classifier and `--force` semantics, with the supplied docs and upgrade-visible evidence serving as the public contract.

options.title: Use a dedicated acknowledgement flag
options.body: Preserve overwrite-only `--force` behavior and add a separate explicit source-risk acknowledgement, accepting an additional CLI surface to reduce semantic coupling.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Land interactive warnings first and defer noninteractive, chat, or Crestodian enforcement until their compatibility expectations are separately approved.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the current trusted-source classifier and `--force` semantics, with the supplied docs and upgrade-visible evidence serving as the public contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent shipped work is adjacent to plugin installation and security controls, providing the strongest available independent history signal for reviewing this permanent boundary.
